headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared filesystem/MCP bridge; no documented pairwise isolation between Continue and mem0.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read/write workspace files and use MCP; its shared state is via filesystem. mem0 has no documented isolation or parsing controls here, so if mem0 ingests Continue-produced content from shared files or MCP, attacker-controlled text could be reinterpreted as instructions. The interaction is plausible in default IDE workflows, though not proven.
conditions: IF mem0 consumes Continue output from a shared file or MCP channel as trusted text
IF Continue writes attacker-influenced content into a workspace file that mem0 later parses
mitigations: Disable shared-file handoff between the agents
Require explicit provenance tags on any file passed from Continue to mem0
Route inter-agent data through a read-only export step
Review MCP server inputs before enabling tool calls
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and can write workspace files; its shared state is via filesystem. mem0’s profile shows no data classes touched, but if it stores or reuses content from the same workspace, sensitive code or buffers can leak across the pair. The pathway exists in default workspace-sharing setups, though mem0’s exact ingestion path is undocumented.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF mem0 persists or re-emits content copied from Continue-managed files
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Restrict Continue to non-sensitive folders
Clear any shared scratch files after each task
Verify mem0 storage scope before enabling shared inputs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on the workspace

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has broad filesystem write and shell capabilities, while mem0 exposes no write or concurrency details. A direct write-write conflict is not evidenced, and mem0’s lack of surfaced mutable resources makes overlap uncertain. Because uncertainty must escalate only when needed, this stays low rather than none due to the shared-filesystem pathway on Continue.
conditions: IF mem0 is configured to write into the same directory Continue edits
IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Use file locks in the orchestrator
Check mem0 for any hidden write targets before deployment

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or facts from editor context, and mem0 is a knowledge-management agent that may store or reuse those outputs. If mem0 treats Continue’s output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into later retrieval or downstream actions. The pairwise pathway is plausible, but no explicit action-taking authority is documented for mem0.
conditions: IF mem0 stores Continue-generated text without validation
IF later workflows retrieve mem0 memory as ground truth for new actions
mitigations: Add a verification step before mem0 persistence
Mark Continue outputs as untrusted by default
Limit mem0 writes to reviewed summaries only
Sample-check stored memories for hallucinations
requires-engineering: add confidence/provenance metadata to memory records

E_compliance.rationale: Continue explicitly touches source code and open editor buffers and handles model-provider API keys, while mem0’s residency, retention, and certification posture are not documented here. No specific residency mismatch is evidenced, so this is a low compliance risk driven by incomplete policy visibility rather than a confirmed breach.
conditions: IF sensitive code or regulated data is routed into mem0 storage
IF mem0 retention or residency differs from the workspace policy
mitigations: Confirm retention settings for both agents
Avoid placing regulated data in shared memory flows
Document data-class handling for each agent
Review vendor terms before enabling shared use
